record_type_quote: To fully understand whether resveratrol activates SIRT1 deacetylase activity, we have used both a peptide substrate lacking the fluorophore and full-length PCG-1a protein in in vitro enzyme assays.

targets.authors: Howitz K.T., Bitterman K.J., Cohen H.Y., Lamming D.W., Lavu S., Wood J.G., Zipkin R.E., Chung P., Kisielewski A., Zhang L.L., Scherer B., Sinclair D.A.
targets.title: Small molecule activators of sirtuins extend Saccharomyces cerevisiae lifespan.
targets.evidence_quote: Molecular screening of SIRT1 activators led to the identification of plant polyphenols as SIRT1 activators, among which is resveratrol (6).
targets.outcome_quote: In conclusion, resveratrol activates SIRT1 only when the Fluor de Lys-SIRT1 peptide substrate was used. We demonstrated that it acts as a SIRT1 substrate exclusively because of the fluorophore on the peptide and therefore, it is not an appropriate SIRT1 substrate.
targets.outcome_reasoning: The original assay effect is obtained, but the central conclusion is that the fluorophore creates an artificial substrate and apparent activation does not establish direct SIRT1 activation. This is the main methodological critique, rather than a minor limitation.

reasoning: New enzyme and cell experiments re-test the direct activation claim attributed to reference 6. The earlier critiques (references 9 and 10) are supporting antecedents, not separate targets; animal metabolic and lifespan findings are not re-tested.
